en: He reckoned the gray wolf favored by fortune
No greater than his ankle.
With every blow, Sarybay
Cracked like lightning,
Clashing with mounting courage,
Bearing the standard across the dark battlefield,
His eyes blazing like a hungry wolf’s.
He girded himself and strained,
Swaying as though about to strike,
Without sorrow or distress,
Without even knitting his brow,
Never crying, “Alas, I am slain!”
Never fearing death,
He barred the road of escape,
Closing it off as he advanced.
All your far-flung insolence.
Let me drive your warriors aside,
Slaughter and burn a multitude of you.
Let me wreak a mighty massacre;
If your Kyrgyz fall into my hands,
I shall leave your braided women widows,
Stain the trap’s jaws with blood,
Turn your black road to dust,
Extinguish the fire you kindle,
And drive every one of you away.
If I do not bring ruin and slaughter,
Roaring in fury,
Churning heaven and sky—
Then I have never been Sarybay,
Nor ever mounted the steed named Sarybay.
Since I matured and became a man,
And stood as an equal among heroes,
Keeping villages and possessing lands,
Inspiring dread and ruling peoples,
No land has remained unseen by me,
No nation has remained unconquered by me;
I slaughtered khans and captured lions.
How many tens of thousands have I conquered!
I have faced many spears and guns
Without ever losing my wits.
Yet never upon the earth have I seen
A youth like this Külchoro.
He is a champion and a hero,
A youth at the height of his strength.
One worthy to trade equal blows—
Ah, now I see: this is my true enemy!
He is a warrior and a lion;
My coming here has brought me torment.
I sought suffering and conflict;
This is the foe destined to fight me.
He is renowned; he is a lion.
For slaughtering my father, the Monster,
And leaving a mound above his grave,
He truly is a hero, if I speak no lie.
He is mighty, and of a khan’s blood;
I shall occupy Talas and settle there.
I shall demolish your stone enclosures
And burn and consume multitudes of you.
I shall seize your noble ones;
Beginning with Aiköl, I shall drain
The blood of every one of you.
I shall turn Jelmayan’s head,
And slaughter earth-born Jelpiniş
Down to the very ground.
I shall seize and slaughter their khans;
These have always been my mortal foes,
So I shall consume them all, leaving none.
I shall tear apart whoever confronts me,
Gnaw whoever crosses my path;
If I do not slaughter all I encounter
And sweep them utterly away,
If I do not seize and conquer your people,
And swallow them all without remainder,
Then rather than remain Sarybay,
May I sink unborn into darkness,
May I die instead of living!
If I do not wreak slaughter among your multitudes,
If I do not plunder your daughters,
If I do not spread carnage to your borders,
Bind your gray-wolf giant,
And smash open your skull,
Then let me draw out
All your far-flung insolence!
Your heroes and your khans
I shall cast into turmoil and slaughter.
Leaving not one of you,
Your nobles and your khans—
I, the warrior Sarybay,
Shall trample every one of you.
I shall make your blood flow like water,
Not sparing a single one of you.
I shall bind your giant alive,
Raid your mares from the uplands,
And pound your brains to pulp;
Then let me draw out
Though you be mighty falcons,
You wretches shall die by my hand.
In my wrath I shall conquer;
Not only your people but your land
I shall swallow when I fix my hostile gaze upon it!
I shall seize every one of you,
Make your blood pour out,
And cut short your precious lives!
I shall shake off your filthy dust.
Felling the trees of your fortune,
Toppling your houses to the ground,
May I die if I do not gather your people as plunder,
Crush your nation to powder,
And slaughter you all cleanly together.
May I die and cease to be Sarybay!”
So declared Sarybay,
And as Sarybay stood there thus,
The times closed in with dreadful force.
He unleashed utter turmoil;
In his fury, Sarybay
Struck Döböchö once.
Sparks flew from his mace,
And fire burst from Döböchö.
As though he would envelop the whole world,
As though he would leave not one
Of those he met unsucked and undevoured,
Sarybay upon his mount
Flared up, the accursed madman.
His eyes blazed like a wolf’s,
And he ground his teeth like a boar;
His thirst for blood seized him.
Power surged from his bearing,
And through the fire of his two cheeks
Black hair sprouted thickly.
He made ready in wrath,
And all delight fled away.
Ah, the warrior who had conquered the world,
The infidel, was filled with rage.
He was madness itself,
One who spilled blood and severed heads,
Just as everyone had long rumored—
He proved to be exactly as they said.
He was a warrior and a lion,
A hero beyond all reckoning.
“I shall scatter their young heroes
And slaughter their Külchoro!”
So declaring, Sarybay
Brandished his many-fashioned spear,
Sweeping it from side to side,
And began a dreadful battle.
He summoned his courage and prepared,
Seeming destined to prevail.
He looked as if he would conquer
The whole wide world.
He seemed about to unleash
A vast and terrible calamity.
Your warrior, the Monster’s son,
Your infidel who scorched the earth,
Unmatched in valor, mighty in venom—
He was that accursed one himself,
The black eye of the demon himself,
Calamity incarnate.
He made ready in wrath,
Set all his weapons in order,
And prepared to enter the fray.
The road before him narrowed,
And his fury became crimson flame.
He roared as he rode toward the ridge,
The fortunate accursed one,
The scorched and raging madman.
He roared menacingly,
And cried out in anger:
“If you mean to come, send your hero!
Send your lion favored by fortune!
Send one skillful with the spear!
Send your strongest, one who will not flinch!
Send the brave man who has girded his waist!
Send your renowned champion and lion!
Behold this might of mine!
Though you fill the earth like the blue sky,
Looming vast as a gorge-riven mountain,
His two eyes bulging,
As though he would suck out any soul he struck,
As though, without a backward glance,
He would slaughter any living being—
Such was Sarybay’s appearance.
His immense weight scorched the earth,
His ferocity scorched the people,
And he began a great upheaval.
The wretch, despairing of life,
Caused many another soul
To perish outright.
Writhing in rage,
The people despaired of their lives,
While divine power struck the madman
With all its force.
Toward Külchoro
He leveled his blue-steel spear.
Before he could arrive ahead of an arrow,
Before he could reach and transfix
The warrior favored by fortune,
His mind crowded with grave fears,
The poor youth beset by many troubles,
The hero Seytek, son of Semetey,
Leveled his spear and charged;
Keeping him from reaching his uncle,
He cast his fly-like life aside.
He too was a falcon and a lion;
His valor and leonine courage
Had now come to the fore.
The playful hero Seytek
Had come out onto the plain
To shield his gray-wolf uncle.
His earliest forefather was Tügöl Khan;
The poor youth’s roots ran deep,
And all his forefathers were khans;
From birth, Kydyr had blessed him.
He was the offspring of my hero.
“That buried swine will reach
My uncle, whose strength is nearly spent,” he thought.
He is the black eye of the demon;
When he strains, he sucks out life,
Calamity incarnate.
Sarybay had turned deadly earnest
And unleashed surpassing fury.
Dust rose everywhere,
And this wretched, faithless world
Seemed utterly overturned.
He lunged in bitter desperation,
Clawing the earth like a polar bear.
Leaning back, he drew his mace,
And when his violent rage seized him,
He seemed capable of shattering the blue sky.
Behold the monstrous Sarybay;
See how his fury raged.
May your renown pass away, cursed raider;
May you die and be laid in the earth.
May your fortunate city be bound,
May you die and be bound beneath the ground.
He advanced, bellowing and snarling,
Clattering in fury,
Making ready like a tiger,
Whose charge none could survive.
He flared up in raging fury,
Changing through countless forms without pause.
He stormed and thundered in wrath,
His towering hair and beard bristling,
As vast as the Üңkür-Koo gorge.
Anyone who entered his reach,
He seemed ready to seize and swallow;
Such was Sarybay’s nature.
Sarybay rode out prepared,
With all his weapons fastened.
Like a returning blast of bitter cold,
Like snow and ice that tormented living souls,
The wretched hero Sarybay,
When you beheld his greatest might,
Was like an icy wind sweeping down the valley.
Raging together with Jelmayan,
He strained as though to swallow and devour,
Lest it be said that he surrendered him to the enemy.
